flags: vcut=-0.1 is numerically inert in this code: eta/exclurad.F line 254 reads 'if(cutv.gt.1d-12)vmax=min(vmax,cutv)'. A negative cutv fails this comparison, so the inelasticity cut is skipped entirely and vmax falls back to its unconstrained kinematic maximum (~0.447 GeV^2 at this point). The run will be identical to vcut=0 (no cut), NOT a cut on v as the README/example comments imply ('negative = cut on v'). I found no code path anywhere in exclurad.F that implements a negative-vcut branch -- the documentation describes a feature that does not exist in this source tree.
explanation: The requested kinematic point (W=1.7 GeV, Q^2=1.0 GeV^2, cos theta*=0, phi*=90 deg) is physically valid for eta electroproduction: W is well above the eta-p threshold (m_p+m_eta=1.486 GeV) and lies inside the tabulated EtaMAID-2023 grid (W: 1.487-2.211 GeV, Q^2: 0.3-5.0 GeV^2, |cos|<=0.9). I generated the input file exactly as requested, including vcut=-0.1. However, tracing the Fortran source shows the vcut=-0.1 setting will NOT apply any inelasticity cut -- the code only applies a cut when cutv > 1e-12, so a negative value silently falls through to the uncut (vmax) integration, equivalent to vcut=0. This contradicts the repo's own documentation, which claims negative vcut cuts directly on v rather than v^2. I proceeded with generation (this is not a physical impossibility, just a documented-but-nonfunctional input option) but flagged the discrepancy so the result is not misinterpreted as having any inelasticity cut applied.
